arxiv-2012-14997.title: Bipartite Leggett-Garg and macroscopic Bell inequality violations using cat states: distinguishing weak and deterministic macroscopic realism
arxiv-2012-14997.creator: Manushan Thenabadu and M. D. Reid 1
arxiv-2012-14997.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Manushan Thenabadu and M. D. Reid 1. We consider tests of Leggett-Garg’s macrorealism and of macroscopic local realism, where for spacelike separated measurements the assumption of macroscopic noninvasive measurability is justified by that of macroscopic locality. We give a mapping between the Bell and Leggett-Garg experiments for microscopic qubits based on spin 1 / 2 1/2 eigenstates and gedanken experiments for macroscopic qubits based on two macroscopically distinct coherent states (cat states).

arxiv-2102-12661.title: Online Learning for Unknown Partially Observable MDPs
arxiv-2102-12661.creator: Mehdi Jafarnia-Jahromi, Rahul Jain, Ashutosh Nayyar
arxiv-2102-12661.description: Abstract Solving Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs) is hard. Learning optimal controllers for POMDPs when the model is unknown is harder. Online learning of optimal controllers for unknown POMDPs, which requires efficient learning using regret-minimizing algorithms that effectively tradeoff exploration and exploitation, is even harder, and no solution exists currently.

arxiv-2107-06261.title: Tight running times for minimum ℓ q \ell_{q} -norm load balancing: beyond exponential dependencies on 1 / ϵ 1/\epsilon
arxiv-2107-06261.creator: Lin Chen Liangde Tao José Verschae
arxiv-2107-06261.description: Abstract We consider a classical scheduling problem on m m identical machines. For an arbitrary constant q > 1 q>1 , the aim is to assign jobs to machines such that ∑ i = 1 m C i q \sum_{i=1}^{m}C_{i}^{q} is minimized, where C i C_{i} is the total processing time of jobs assigned to machine i i .

arxiv-2108-03971.title: Lottery paradox, DNA evidence and other stories: How to accept uncertain statements
arxiv-2108-03971.creator: Yudi Pawitan
arxiv-2108-03971.description: Abstract I think we can agree that dealing with uncertainty is not easy. Probability is the main tool for dealing with uncertainty, and we know there are many probability-related puzzles and paradoxes. Here I describe a rather idiosyncratic selection that highlights the problem of accepting uncertain statements.

arxiv-2406-06687.title: CombineHarvesterFlow : Joint Probe Analysis Made Easy with Normalizing Flows
arxiv-2406-06687.creator: Peter L. Taylor, Andrei Cuceu, Chun-Hao To, Erik A. Zaborowski
arxiv-2406-06687.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Peter L. Taylor, Andrei Cuceu, Chun-Hao To, Erik A. Zaborowski. We show how to efficiently sample the joint posterior of two non-covariant experiments with a large set of nuisance parameters. Specifically, we train an ensemble of normalizing flows to learn the posterior distribution of both experiments.

arxiv-2410-06686.title: Thermomajorization Mpemba Effect
arxiv-2410-06686.creator: Tan Van Vu, Hisao Hayakawa
arxiv-2410-06686.description: Abstract The Mpemba effect is a counterintuitive physical phenomenon where a hot system cools faster than a warm one. In recent years, theoretical analyses of the Mpemba effect have been developed for microscopic systems and experimentally verified. However, the conventional theory relies on a specific choice of distance measure to quantify relaxation speed, leading to several theoretical ambiguities.

arxiv-2410-22468.title: frb-voe : A Real-time Virtual Observatory Event Alert Service for Fast Radio Bursts
arxiv-2410-22468.creator: Thomas C. Abbott, Andrew V. Zwaniga, Charanjot Brar, Victoria M. Kaspi, Emily Petroff, Mohit Bhardwaj, P.J. Boyle, Amanda M. Cook, Ronniy C. Joseph, Kiyoshi W. Masui, Ayush Pandhi, Ziggy Pleunis, Paul Scholz, Kaitlyn Shin, Shriharsh Tendulkar
arxiv-2410-22468.description: Abstract We present frb-voe , a publicly available software package that enables radio observatories to broadcast fast radio burst (FRB) alerts to subscribers through low-latency virtual observatory events (VOEvents). We describe a use-case of frb-voe by the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment Fast Radio Burst (CHIME/FRB) Collaboration, which has broadcast thousands of FRB alerts to subscribers worldwide.

arxiv-2502-11703.title: CMQCIC-Bench: A Chinese Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Medical Quality Control Indicator Calculation Thanks: Corresponding authors.
arxiv-2502-11703.creator: Guangya Yu, Yanhao Li, Zongying Jiang, Yuxiong Jin, Li Dai, Yupian Lin
arxiv-2502-11703.description: Abstract Medical quality control indicators are essential to assess the qualifications of healthcare institutions for medical services. With the impressive performance of large language models (LLMs) like GPT-4 in the medical field, leveraging these technologies for the M edical Q uality C ontrol I ndicator C alculation (MQCIC) presents a promising approach.

arxiv-2503-17995.title: A Multi-Affine Geometric Framework for Quantum Nonlocality: Unifying Berry Phases, Entanglement, and Coherence
arxiv-2503-17995.creator: Shoshauna Gauvin
arxiv-2503-17995.description: Abstract We relate Berry-phase control and retained entropy geometry to recoverable coherence, entanglement, and Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) correlations. For a depolarized Bell pair subject to recorded phase noise, we determine exact CHSH optima when Bob retains his record and when he compresses it with his qubit into one qubit by any deterministic quantum channel.

arxiv-2504-01429.title: Refining Interactions: Enhancing Anisotropy in Graph Neural Networks with Language Semantics
arxiv-2504-01429.creator: Zhaoxing Li, Haifeng Zhang, Xiaoming Zhang, Chengxiang Liu
arxiv-2504-01429.description: Abstract The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) has recently been explored to enhance the capabilities of Text Attribute Graphs (TAGs). Most existing methods feed textual descriptions of the graph structure or neighbouring nodes’ text directly into LLMs.

arxiv-2504-11569.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Decentralized Reservoir Management via Murmuration Intelligence
arxiv-2504-11569.creator: Heming Fu 1 , Guojun Xiong 2 , Jian Li 1 , Shan Lin 1
arxiv-2504-11569.description: Abstract . Conventional centralized water management systems face critical limitations from computational complexity and uncertainty propagation. We present MurmuRL , a novel decentralized framework inspired by starling murmurations intelligence, integrating bio-inspired alignment , separation , and cohesion rules with multi-agent reinforcement learning. MurmuRL enables individual reservoirs to make autonomous local decisions while achieving emergent global coordination.

arxiv-2507-12013.title: QAS-QTNs: Curriculum Reinforcement Learning-Driven Quantum Architecture Search for Quantum Tensor Networks
arxiv-2507-12013.creator: Siddhant Dutta 1 , Nouhaila Innan 2,3 , Sadok Ben Yahia 4,5 , Muhammad Shafique 2,3
arxiv-2507-12013.description: Abstract Quantum Architecture Search (QAS) is an emerging field aimed at automating the design of quantum circuits for optimal performance. This paper introduces a novel QAS framework employing hybrid quantum reinforcement learning with quantum curriculum learning strategies, enabling learning agents to tackle increasingly complex quantum circuit design tasks.

arxiv-2509-25259.title: A Synthetic Theory of Socio-Epistemic Structuration: Capital, Ideology, and Agency in the Age of Digital Inequality
arxiv-2509-25259.creator: Ricardo Alonzo Fernández Salguero
arxiv-2509-25259.description: Abstract This article proposes a synthetic theory of socio-epistemic structuration to understand the reproduction of inequality in contemporary societies. I argue that social reality is not only determined by material structures and social networks but is fundamentally shaped by the epistemic frameworks—ideologies, narratives, and attributions of agency—that mediate actors’ engagement with their environment.

arxiv-2602-22171.title: A Taxonomy of Human–MLLM Interaction in Early-Stage Sketch-Based Design Ideation Conference: Extended Abstracts of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; April 13–17, 2026; Barcelona, Spain Extended Abstracts of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (C
arxiv-2602-22171.creator: Weiyan Shi, Kenny Tsu Wei Choo
arxiv-2602-22171.description: Abstract . As multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are increasingly integrated into early-stage design tools, it is important to understand how designers collaborate with AI during ideation. In a user study with 12 participants, we analysed sketch-based design interactions with an MLLM-powered system using automatically recorded interaction logs and post-task interviews.

britannica-1911-mequinez.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-mequinez.description: Article 'Mequinez' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 18), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. richly carved and painted woodwork in Mauresque style. The walls are tiled to a height of 4 or 5 ft., and above they are finished in plaster, whitewashed or carved into filigree work. The population numbers being between thirty and forty thousand. Idrisi, writing in A.D. 1100, calls the place Takarart, and describes it as an ordinary citadel, from which the town gradually developed, taking its name from the Miknasa Berbers.

pmc-10731556.title: Quality of life and swallowing outcomes after early proactive swallowing rehabilitation by either transcutaneous neuromuscular electrical stimulation or exercise‐based swallowing training in patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma after radiotherapy
pmc-10731556.creator: Peter K. M. Ku, Alexander C. Vlantis, Rita W. M. Wong, Thomas S. C. Hui, Thomas Law, Louisa K. Y. Ng, Eddy W. Y. Wong, W. T. Chang, David R. Johnson, Florence S. T. Mok, K. H. Wong, Victor Abdullah, Andrew van Hasselt, Kathy Y. S. Lee, Michael C. F. Tong
pmc-10731556.description: BackgroundExercise‐based swallowing training (EBST) and transcutaneous neuromuscular electrical stimulation (TNMES) are common modalities used to treat late dysphagia after radiotherapy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). We aimed to investigate and compare the efficacies of EBST and TNMES as proactive treatments administered early after radiotherapy.MethodsPatients with early post‐radiotherapy NPC (n = 120) underwent either TNMES or EBST.

pmc-11494207.title: Investigating the interplay between the mir-183/182/96 cluster and the adherens junction pathway in early-stage breast cancer
pmc-11494207.creator: Tala Noun, Abdallah Kurdi, Nour Maatouk, Rabih Talhouk, Heinrich zu Dohna
pmc-11494207.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Although the miR-183/182/96 cluster is overexpressed in breast cancer (BC), little is known about its role in the development of pre-carcinogenic lesions which harbor disrupted adherens junctions (AJ) and may promote BC. Here, we used microRNA and RNA sequencing data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) Breast Cancer project to investigate the relationship between the miR-183/182/96 cluster and AJ signaling in early-stage BC.

pmc-11691721.title: BEYOND BORDERS: LONG-DISTANCE CAREGIVING AND SLEEP HABITS IN SOUTH ASIAN COMMUNITIES
pmc-11691721.creator: Aziza Siddiqui, Srujana Chekuri, Akankshya Chataut, Dinesh Karki, Julie Blaskewicz Boron
pmc-11691721.description: Caregiving is generally altruistic in South Asian (SA) communities; however, caregiving activities can still create significant strain for caregivers depending on situational factors, including sleep and built environments (Hossain et al., 2020). Particularly, long-distance caregivers may grapple with the added complexities of not being physically present to provide care.

pmc-11745033.title: An Instrument for Evaluating the Self: The Self-Discrepancies Scale in Non-Clinical Participants
pmc-11745033.creator: Martine Bouvard, Arnaud Carré, Nathalie Fournet, Céline Douilliez, Céline Baeyens, Pierre Philippot
pmc-11745033.description: ObjectiveThe Self-Discrepancies Scale (S-DS) is a multiple-subscore instrument designed to assess discrepancies between mental representations of the self: the actual self on one hand, and the ideal and socially prescribed selves on the other. Its idiographic subscores rely on the endorsement of self-descriptive traits, while its abstract subscores form an overall judgement of felt self-discrepancies.

pmc-12469367.title: Pterostilbene Eliminates MRSA Independent of Metabolic State and Effectively Prevents Biofilm Formation in Milk Matrices
pmc-12469367.creator: Xiaoyong Huang, Huiting Yang, Chenli Wang, Shiqi Yan, Xiaomin Ren, Zilong Sun
pmc-12469367.description: The relentless spread of antimicrobial resistance poses a severe threat to global public health, food safety, and environmental security. Natural products with potent antimicrobial activity offer prospective substitutes for traditional antibiotics and chemical preservatives. Here, we demonstrate that pterostilbene (PT), a natural dietary compound, exhibits rapid lytic activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).

pmc-12508152.title: The prognostic importance of left ventricular diastolic function in primary mitral regurgitation and its relation to structural changes by CMR
pmc-12508152.creator: Hossam Lababidi, Kinan Carlos El-Tallawi, Danai Kitkungvan, Clara L. Angulo, Dipan J. Shah, William A. Zoghbi, Sherif F. Nagueh
pmc-12508152.description: Patients with significant primary mitral regurgitation (MR) can develop left ventricular (LV) diastolic dysfunction (DD). We sought to study LV structural correlates, and prognostic significance of DD. Patients with ≥ moderate primary MR with echocardiographic and CMR scans within a median time of 5 days were included.

pmc-12650004.title: Association Between Heavy Metals Exposure and Elevated High-Sensitivity C-Reactive Protein: Mediating Role of Body Mass Index
pmc-12650004.creator: Seong-Uk Baek, Jin-Ha Yoon, Iogann Tolbatov
pmc-12650004.description: Heavy metal exposure is linked to obesity and systemic inflammation. This study explored the mediating role of body mass index (BMI) in the association of heavy metal exposure with high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP). Blood levels of mercury (Hg), cadmium (Cd), and lead (Pb) were assessed in a nationwide sample of 4521 adults.

pmc-12671272.title: Moisture‐Enabled Electricity Generation from a Single‐Layer Composite CNT‐Polymer Membrane
pmc-12671272.creator: Ioanna Tzoumani, Konstantinos C. Andrikopoulos, Amaia Soto Beobide, Joannis K. Kallitsis
pmc-12671272.description: Clean and renewable power sources are crucial toward the development of sustainable energy technologies, to address the global energy demand. Moisture‐enabled electricity generators (MEGs) have emerged as promising candidates to harness ambient low‐grade energy stored in the humidity of the atmosphere.

pmc-12964932.title: Evaluation of the updated 2022 lung-GPA in NSCLC adenocarcinoma patients with brain metastases: analysis of prognostic factors in a German clinical cohort
pmc-12964932.creator: Niklas Mittenbacher, Jens Christian Philippi, Dirk Vordermark, Daniel Medenwald, Jörg Andreas Müller
pmc-12964932.description: BackgroundLung cancer is the most frequent source of brain metastases (BMs), with 20-40% of patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) developing BMs during the course of disease. The NSCLC-GPA (Graded Prognostic Assessment), developed by Sperduto et al., aims to estimate overall survival (OS) in lung cancer patients with BMs based on multiple prognostic factors.

pmc-13508166.title: Metal carcinogens and cancer: integrating genetic and epigenetic perspectives
pmc-13508166.creator: Shipra Singh, Priyanka Phogat, Luciano Saso, Shrikant Kukreti, Aparna Bansal
pmc-13508166.description: People around the globe are affected by extensive environmental and occupational exposure to heavy metals, which poses a significant threat to various health hazards, with cancer being a major concern. These toxic metals are ubiquitously found in food, air, water, and industrial, agricultural, or pharmaceutical applications. Being non-biodegradable, they accumulate in the living organism.

pmc-13540896.title: Transformer-accelerated discovery of inhibitors targeting the RpsAΔ438 deletion in PZA-resistant tuberculosis
pmc-13540896.creator: Jiazhuo Xiao, Muhammad Shahab, Haoke Zhang, Zunnan Huang

pmc-13670182.title: Revisiting Identification Thresholds of Specific Learning Disorders (SLD) in Gifted Children (GC). A Comparison of Three Groups: Twice‐Exceptional (TE) Children, GC Without SLD and Non‐GC With SLD
pmc-13670182.creator: Laurent Lesecq, Laurent Querne, Julie Gornes, Laura Buffo, Louise Corbel, Loïse Perrais, Maëlys Kartner, Anne Gaelle Le Moing, Beatrice Bourdin, Patrick Berquin
pmc-13670182.description: This study investigates assessment of Specific Learning Disorders (SLD) in Twice‐Exceptional (TE) children, gifted children (GC) who also present SLD, in oral and written language domains. Applying the standard threshold for identification (< 7th percentile) to GC often results in the assessment and identification of SLD in the TE population, thereby limiting access to appropriate support.
